answer: I would like to talk about my closest friend, whom I have known since our very first week at university, so roughly seven years now. We were both studying business administration and were placed in the same project group, and something just clicked almost immediately, probably because we were both from small towns and slightly overwhelmed by the big campus. By the end of that first term we were sharing notes, meals and far too many cups of tea. Over the years our lives have taken very different directions, yet the friendship has proved remarkably [[durable]]. He now works for a bank in Dhaka, while I am still in Sirajganj, so we do not actually see each other often, but whenever we meet it feels as though no time has passed. When we do manage to meet, we usually go for long walks by the river or watch a cricket match together, and in between we talk on the phone most weekends. I think what has kept us close is a shared sense of humour and a kind of [[unspoken]] understanding that we will always be there for each other. He is the one person I can be completely [[candid]] with, without fear of judgement. What I value most is that our friendship has never felt like hard work; it is genuinely [[effortless]]. Honestly, in a world where people drift apart so easily, having one friendship that has lasted this long feels like something worth protecting, and I hope we are still arguing about cricket when we are old men.

followUps.q: Do you think you will stay friends in the future?
followUps.answer: I am fairly sure we will. We have already survived distance and busy jobs, so I cannot imagine much that would pull us apart now. If anything, the friendship keeps [[deepening]] as we get older.

followUps.q: How do you usually keep in touch?
followUps.answer: Mostly through phone calls and messages. We have a habit of calling each other on Friday evenings, and even if it is only for ten minutes, it keeps us up to date with each other's lives.

note: Fixed 'roughly ten years' to 'seven years' (mid-20s persona); added BBA detail, his job in Dhaka, what we do together and a light closing line.
